item.title: The Containment Polytope of a Triangle and a Convex Polygon
item.description: arXiv:2611.08556v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The containment polytope $\mathcal{C}$ for a triangle $P$ and a convex $n$-gon $Q$ is a four-dimensional polytope representing the similarity transforms (translation, rotation, scaling) that place $P$ inside $Q$. While it is known that the complexity of $\mathcal{C}$ and its silhouette $\Lambda$, which represents all the largest placements of $P$ inside $Q$ for all orientations, can be quadratic in $n$, we show that the silhouette can be partitioned into a linear number of planar convex chains and steps in $O(n \log n)$ time. Based on the linear number of convex chains and steps, we can compute the complexity of silhouette $\Lambda$ in $O(n \log n)$ time and query the largest placement of $P$ inside $Q$ for a given orientation in $O(\log n)$ time. We explain geometrically how the triangle $P$ rotates while continuously scaling and translating to be maximal inside $Q$, leading to a parameterized algorithm for containment problems.
item.dc:creator: Yoonsung Choi, Sunghee Choi

item.title: Containment Problems in Convex Sets
item.description: arXiv:2611.08835v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $P$ be a set of $n$ points in the plane, and let $C$ be a compact, convex subset of the plane that contains the origin in its interior. We study the problem of finding two points $p$ and $q$ of $P$ with the property that any homothet of $C$ that contains $p$ and $q$ must contain at least a constant fraction of the points of $P$. We give proofs for several cases. When $C$ is strictly convex we achieve a fraction of $1/5$, and when $C$ is a general convex region we achieve a fraction of $1/6e$. We show how the ideas of this second bound can be used to prove a lower bound for a version of the problem in $\mathbb{R}^d$ when $C$ is a $d$-ball. We also consider a few special cases. When $C$ is a triangle we get a lower bound of $1/12$, and when we allow that triangle to be rotated by $\pi$ radians in addition to being scaled and translated we get a lower bound of $1/768$. In proving this last result, we improve the state of the art on the version of this problem in three dimensions, where $C$ is a parallelepiped. We also consider the algorithmic aspects of finding such a pair of points.
item.dc:creator: Prosenjit Bose, Bobby Miraftab, Tyler Tuttle

item.title: Separating Measures by Hyperplanes
item.description: arXiv:2611.09166v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Given red and blue points in $\mathbb{R}^d$, connect every red point to every blue point and weigh each segment by its length under a fixed norm. What fraction of the total weight can always be captured by a single affine hyperplane separating the segments' endpoints? We study this question for finite point configurations in affine general position and, more generally, for pairs of probability measures. For dimension one, we show that choosing the best of three thresholds determined by the means of the two distributions captures at least one third of the total red-blue distance. We also give a matching upper bound. Embedding the line construction to higher dimensions shows that the guarantee of $1/3$ cannot be improved for arbitrary measures. Thus, we pivot to the family of measures whose atoms are in affine general position and whose non-atomic part places zero mass on all hyperplanes. Crucially, we establish that the worst-case guarantee is identical for finite configurations in affine general position and several natural classes of probability measures, thereby unifying the discrete and continuous formulations of the problem. For this family of measures and for higher dimensions, we extend our guarantee of $1/3$ for all norms. Our proofs combine the ham-sandwich theorem with a novel coupling argument and, in the planar case, an integral representation of norms. We also show that the optimal guarantee improves as the dimension grows, giving a lower bound of $1/2-\operatorname{O}\left(1/\sqrt{d}\right)$ as well as an asymptotically matching upper bound of $1/2$ for every $d$. For the Euclidean distance, we refine the lower bounds to $8/(8+5\pi)$ and $1/2-\operatorname{O}\left(1/d\right)$ and, for $d=2$, the upper bound to $5/11$. We also derive dimension-dependent guarantees for finite point configurations, including perfect separation of $n$ points of each color when $d\geq2n-1$.
item.dc:creator: Jos\'e Correa, Svenja M. Griesbach, Elfarouk Harb, Felix Hommelsheim, Reda Jlibene, Vasilis Livanos, Eilon Solan

item.title: Bourgain's Theorem for a Union of Euclidean Metric Spaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.08546v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the distortion of embedding a union of $k$ Euclidean sets into Euclidean space. We show that a union of $k$ Euclidean sets can be embedded with distortion at most $O(k^{1.128} \log k)$, independent of the number of points. This is an exponential improvement over the previous best known upper bound of $2^{O(k)}$ obtained by iterating the result of Makarychev and Makarychev (2016) for the special case $k = 2$. Surprisingly, with the additional assumption that each Euclidean set remains Euclidean when we adjoin any other two points, we can obtain an asymptotically tight distortion of $O(\log k)$, thus, providing a generalization of Bourgain's Theorem (1985). Along the way, we also show that the distortion of the union can be upper bounded by $O(\log k)$ times the maximum of the Lipschitz extension constants of individual Euclidean sets.
item.dc:creator: Dimitar Chakarov, Sepideh Mahabadi, Yury Makarychev, Ali Vakilian

item.title: Coresets for Capacitated Clustering via Dual Concentration
item.description: arXiv:2611.09600v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study coresets for clustering problems, focusing on the classical $k$-median and $k$-means objectives. A coreset is a small weighted summary of the input data that approximately preserves the clustering cost for every choice of centers. Such summaries are a central tool for scaling clustering algorithms to large datasets. In this work, we consider the capacitated setting, where the clustering is subject not only to choosing centers but also to respecting prescribed cluster-size constraints. This model is a natural generalization of standard clustering and has been widely studied, but its coreset complexity is less well understood. For finite metric spaces, we obtain optimal-size coresets; surprisingly, these match the best-known bounds for unconstrained clustering. We also give improved coreset bounds in Euclidean space, notably the first coresets with near-linear dependence in $k$ while being independent of the dimension and input size. The main new technical ingredients are concentration bounds for the dual solutions of min-cost flow problems, which allow for both significantly simpler and tighter analyses of the underlying sampling distribution used in the coreset construction.
item.dc:creator: Milind Prabhu, Chris Schwiegelshohn, Sudarshan Shyam, Erik Waingarten

item.title: New persistent chain spaces: identifying and computing the relevant persistent Laplacians of a filtration
item.description: arXiv:2611.09610v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Persistent homology (PH) summarizes the topological features of data that persist across scales, but it is insensitive to many geometric properties. Persistent Laplacians (PLs) address this limitation: for a pair of simplicial complexes in a filtration, the kernel of the persistent Laplacian recovers the persistent Betti number, while its non-zero spectrum carries additional geometric information. However, PLs are defined for individual pairs of filtration values, so analysing a whole filtration requires evaluating many operators that largely contain the same information, and the result is hard to summarize and interpret. In this paper, we show that this redundancy has a precise structure. For each pair of filtration values, we decompose the space of chains underlying the persistent up-Laplacian into the contributions inherited from the neighboring pairs and a remaining part, which we call the new persistent chain space. We show that the new persistent chain spaces of all earlier pairs form a direct sum decomposition of this space, so that every persistent up-Laplacian in the filtration is determined by them. Moreover, the new persistent chain spaces are non-trivial only at pairs given by the persistence pairing in the same and in the next homological dimension, so that the persistence pairing determines exactly where the persistent up-Laplacian can change. Experiments on several types of point clouds show that evaluating persistent Laplacians only at these pairs reduces the computation time, both for our implementation and for existing software.
item.dc:creator: Joris Kirchner, Martina Vittorietti

item.title: Multiscale Closing Index (MCI) for measuring structural similarity between 2D point sets
item.description: arXiv:2611.09745v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We introduce Multi-scale Closing Index (MCI), a new dissimilarity measure for evaluating the alignment of two 2D point sets. MCI is bounded between 0 and 1 and is based on multiscale mathematical morphology operations, with smaller values indicating greater structural agreement. The measure was motivated by the need to assess the quality of registration between point sets representing cell populations in biological images. To evaluate its behaviour under controlled conditions, we generated synthetic point clouds from Perlin-noise-based spatial structures, following established approaches for simulating biologically plausible spatial organization. We assessed MCI between those point clouds and different transformed versions, obtained by local perturbation, point removal, translation, rotation and addition of impulsive noise. Across these experiments, the dissimilarity MCI increased gradually and consistently with perturbation severity, while showing a clear discontinuity between clouds originating from the same underlying spatial structure and point clouds generated from different structures. We further compared MCI with commonly used point-set distances, including Hausdorff-based measures and Sliced Wasserstein distance. These experiments show the ability of MCI to capture structural agreement and quantify deviations between point sets, highlighting its potential as a complementary metric for evaluating two-dimensional point-set registration.
item.dc:creator: Nicol\`o Zava, Angel Franco-Alvarez, Samy Blusseau, Santiago Velasco-Forero, Maria-Jose Jimenez

item.title: Sloan's Analytical G\"omb\"oc: Strict Convexity Narrows the Admissible $\beta$ Range
item.description: arXiv:2604.17120v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Varkonyi and Domokos (2006) proved that convex homogeneous bodies with exactly one stable and one unstable equilibrium point exist. Sloan (2023) gave the first analytical parameterization, with radial function $R(\theta,\phi)$ having exactly two critical points on $S^2$. This is the v3 amendment-of-record of arXiv:2604.17120 (v3 corrects an attribution in the v2 title and abstract; no finding changes). v1 claimed Sloan's parameterization does not produce mono-monostatic bodies and reported a 13-member catalog of Fourier/radial extensions certified at ECS=1 via mesh-vertex drainage-basin analysis. Following correspondence with P. L. Varkonyi (BME), an analytical verification suite was built around the Varkonyi-Gauss identity. Finding 1: Sloan's parameterization does produce mono-monostatic bodies in a strictly-convex sub-regime ($\beta\lesssim 0.036$), where $K_{\min} > 0$ and the identity certifies ECS=1. v1 missed this because its mesh-vertex oracle over-counted on shallow COM-height landscapes. Sloan states that $\beta \le 0.17$ should suffice for convexity, but at $\beta=0.05$, inside that range, strict convexity is lost ($K_{\min}=-0.569$; $K<0$ over 4.01% of surface) and the identity's precondition fails. v1's "global surface information" mechanism is replaced by the strict-convexity precondition. Finding 2: Of v1's 13 catalog instances only Phase-1 ($\beta=0.023149$, $a_1=0.234433$, $k=1$) survives identity-based verification; the remaining twelve were per-$k$ optimizer extrema overshooting the strict-convex boundary. Probing the regime interior verifies further mono-monostatic bodies in $k=2$ and $k=3$ sub-families: the verified set is an open regime in $(\beta, a_1, k)$, not a discrete list. Finding 3: v1's ECS=1 readings for the 9 radial-family members reflected drainage-basin merging; the $r=0.9993$ gentleness-robustness correlation is retracted.
item.dc:creator: Vincent Wesley Couey

item.title: Two-colour crossing minimization in complete geometric graphs is NP-hard
item.description: arXiv:2610.31719v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Given a fixed straight-line drawing of a complete graph, we seek a two-colouring of its edges that minimizes monochromatic crossing pairs. We prove that the threshold decision problem is NP-complete, even for points in general position with integer coordinates. Thus exact minimization is NP-hard, resolving the complexity question posed at the Crossing Number Workshop in 2019. We reduce from MaxCut on permutation graphs by representing source vertices with classes of geometric edges, whose crossings encode source adjacencies. The target complete graph also contains every other edge between its points, and their freely chosen colours can affect the encoded cost. To control these interactions, we construct a large comparison grid with two stable colour phases and use program points to turn this reference into colour preferences on other edges. The optimum differs from a computable baseline plus the amplified minimum number of uncut source edges by an error small enough to distinguish consecutive source values. The reduction is deterministic, with polynomially many points and polynomial coordinate bit length.
item.dc:creator: Zhe Zhang, Yi Liu, Dan Yang
